A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 18 pages of v2 and 16 pages of v3, including appendices, are readable; corresponding text, equations, figures, and tables can be matched despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-model fine-tuning experiments, Gaussian-mixture simulations, and forgetting analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds conversational-capability evaluation on AlpacaEval in Appendix A.6.

M1.justification: The SFT, Self-SFT, GRPO, REINFORCE, Iterative-SFT, and RL-trace SFT procedures are retained. The added evaluation and clarified training-duration description do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix A.6 adds AlpacaEval conversational-capability evaluation for Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct and Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct after training on IFEval, MMLU, and Countdown. This extends non-target task coverage while retaining the previous datasets and simulation scenarios.

E2.justification: The existing fine-tuning comparator sets remain unchanged. The new AlpacaEval evaluation explicitly introduces GPT-4 as the reference opponent for win-rate comparisons in Appendix A.6.

E3.justification: The added AlpacaEval experiment evaluates initial, SFT, and RL models using win rate (%) against GPT-4, introducing a protocol for conversational evaluation. Previously reported splits, training settings, and evaluation metrics are retained.

E4.justification: The full learning-rate simulation in v2 Figure 5 survives as v3 Figure 8. Distance sensitivity, KL and advantage ablations, RL-trace SFT, and KL-forgetting correlation analyses are also retained. AlpacaEval adds benchmark coverage rather than a new ablation or diagnostic analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed summaries, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and v3 introduces none for AlpacaEval. The statistical estimation described for the Appendix A.5 correlation analysis is unchanged.

E6.justification: Existing numerical results are retained. New Table 3 reports AlpacaEval outcomes: after Countdown training, initial/SFT/RL win rates are 41.6/0.0/42.0% for Llama-3.1-8B and 36.5/0.4/34.6% for Qwen-2.5-7B. These are newly reported evaluations, not improvements over corresponding v2 scores.

T1.justification: The KL formulations, Gaussian-mixture and overlap definitions in Section 3, and total-variation derivation in Appendix A.2 are unchanged apart from formatting. No mathematical correction or new proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the claims that RL forgets less than SFT, on-policy data explains this robustness, and approximately on-policy data can mitigate forgetting efficiently. Rewritten contribution bullets reorganize these existing claims without materially changing their scope.

C2.justification: The mechanism explanations, scaling and theoretical limitations, and distant-target failure condition remain unchanged. Appendix A.6 reports another instance of the existing empirical pattern; the new impact statement restates safety and continual-learning implications and adds a generic dual-use caveat.

D1.justification: The Figure 7 caption newly states that Iterative-SFT runs for multiple rounds until target accuracy matches SFT, while explaining the fixed two-epoch baseline lines. This clarifies the existing experiment rather than establishing a rerun. Appendix A.3 implementation details and the code-access link are retained.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning relative to prior and concurrent research are retained, including the discussions of Lai et al. and Shenfeld et al. Bibliographic formatting changes do not introduce new research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the contribution bullets, expands the Figure 7 explanation, adds an impact statement and Appendix A.6, and updates conference and correspondence text. Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact; the simulation learning-rate discussion moves to Appendix A.1.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from single-column to two-column conference formatting, substantially altering figure sizes, placement, captions, and page composition. Figure 5 becomes a two-panel display while its original three-panel comparison is retained as Appendix Figure 8. Table 3 is added, and subsequent appendix figures are renumbered.

improvement.justification: Appendix A.6 adds useful evidence that the retention advantage extends to conversational capability, and the Figure 7 caption makes training-duration comparisons clearer. Existing evidence is preserved through the presentation changes. These are limited gains: the new evaluation omits sample counts and detailed judging settings, and the underlying methods and theoretical analysis remain unchanged.
